About

Héctor Jiménez is a Spanish violist based in Leipzig, where he studies at the Hochschule für Musik und Theater «Felix Mendelssohn Bartholdy» in the class of Sara Kim, having begun his studies there with Pauline Sachse.

He trained in Madrid at the Conservatorio Profesional de Música «Victoria de los Ángeles» with Raquel Tavira, and took private lessons with Jaime Huertas, violist of the Cuarteto Leonor. He played solo viola with the Youth Camerata of Madrid and the Youth Orchestra of Madrid (JORCAM). Early recognition came in chamber music and new music: first prize at the National Chamber Music Competition «Ciudad de Ávila» (2021) and, at the Bundesfinale of Jugend musiziert, a second prize in viola solo and a third in early music (2022), followed by a third prize in new music (2023).

His work is centred on contemporary music, an interest that took shape in composition and music theory lessons with José Luis Torá, composer and student of Helmut Lachenmann. His repertoire includes works by Morton Feldman, Salvatore Sciarrino, Mark Andre, Liza Lim and Luciano Berio, as well as premieres of pieces by younger composers; in 2023 he gave a solo concert of Feldman’s The Viola in My Life.

He has developed this repertoire at the Lucerne Festival Academy, at the Essen Now Festival with Studio Musikfabrik, at the World New Music Days with Concrète Lab Ensemble, at the Messiaen-Tage with Ensemble Écoute and in masterclasses with Garth Knox, Stephen Upshaw, Tatjana Masurenko, Rachel Koblyakov and Dejana Sekulić, among others.

In Leipzig he plays regularly with the Philharmonie Leipzig, in a wide range of repertoire and styles that includes film music, symphonic gothic rock concerts and the traditional symphonic repertoire, and takes part in Fabien Lévy’s composition seminar.
